&1&2&3&4\\ \hline

\text{Back upper}&\text{grey}&\text{grey}&\text{dark}&\text{white}\\
\text{Back lower}&?&?&?&\text{dark}
\end{array}
\]

Focus on the dark piece:

1. The visible dark cube in the upper back layer is in column \(3\).
2. Its only possible neighbouring dark cube is directly below it, in the lower back layer, since its other neighbours are grey or white.

4. The dark piece needs a fourth cube. The only unused cube adjacent to these three is in the lower back layer, column \(2\).

Thus the dark piece has the arrangement

\[
\begin{array}{cccc}
\cdot&\cdot&\blacksquare&\cdot\\
\cdot&\blacksquare&\blacksquare&\blacksquare
\end{array}
\]

which is a T-shape. Rotating it \(90^\circ\) gives three cubes in a vertical line with one cube attached to the middle, matching Shape C.
